items.text: Decisions about local schools, roads and services should mostly be made by local communities, not a national authority.
items.rationale: Subsidiarity view held by federalists, localists, communitarians and libertarians; a standing rule judged equally for an ideal design or today's country.

items.text: Any region should be free to leave the country it belongs to if its people choose.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Strong right-of-secession stance (regionalist, anarchist, paleolibertarian, self-determination traditions); concrete constitutional rule in both frames, likely to split by frame for some.

items.text: Regions and local communities should raise and spend most of their own public money.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Fiscal federalism as endorsed by federalists and decentralist left and right; avoids naming any tax system so it reads in any country and any ideal.

items.text: Larger bodies should hold only the powers that local communities agree to pass up to them.
items.rationale: Bottom-up confederal principle shared by anarchists, libertarian municipalists, confederalists and some Catholic subsidiarity thinkers; agentless, so anarchists can agree.

items.text: If people across the country disagree deeply on a moral question, each region should be able to settle it for itself.
items.rationale: Condition (deep disagreement) favours decentralists; endorsed by federalists on both left and right; plausible frame split where today's divisions differ from the ideal.

items.text: If a national rule fits local conditions badly, a region should be able to opt out of it.
items.rationale: Condition (poor local fit) favours decentralists; reflects localist and federalist practice of opt-outs; reads naturally in both frames.

items.text: If a national authority overrides a region's own elected decisions, the region should be entitled to refuse to comply.
items.rationale: Strong nullification/resistance stance (states'-rights, regionalist, autonomist traditions); condition favours the decentralised pole and invites different answers here-and-now versus ideal.

items.text: Most laws should be the same in every part of the country, wherever people live.
items.rationale: Legal uniformity valued by unitarists, civic republicans, many socialists and nationalists; a standing rule meaningful in both frames.

items.text: Any powers held by regions should be on loan from the national centre, which can take them back at any time.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Strong unitary-sovereignty view (Jacobin, unitary-monarchist, democratic-centralist traditions); mirrors fed-04 in extremity; clear in both frames.

items.text: Major public services like health care and schooling should be run as one national system rather than region by region.
items.rationale: National-system view held by social democrats, unitarists and nationalists; mirrors fed-01 and fed-03; works whether today's services are central or regional.

items.text: One central authority should have the final say over every part of the country.
items.rationale: Strong centralist stance shared by unitary monarchists, Jacobin republicans and one-nation nationalists; silent on who that authority is, so it does not load on dem.

items.text: If a region's laws treat a minority unfairly, the national authority should be able to overrule them.
items.rationale: Condition (local injustice) favours centralists; endorsed by civil-rights liberals and unitarists; strong candidate for frame divergence depending on local record.

items.text: If a crisis hits many regions at once, one central body should direct the response for the whole country.
items.rationale: Condition (widespread crisis) favours centralists; coordination argument used by technocrats, nationalists and social democrats; spec stipulates the ideal still meets crises, so it reads in both frames.

items.text: If a region refuses to follow national law, the national authority should be able to take over running it.
items.rationale: Strong direct-rule stance, mirror of fed-07; endorsed by unitarists and national-unity conservatives; plausible frame split where current regional conflicts exist.
